title: French Toast Casserole
shortDescription: Feed the hall before the bell
subtitle: Feed the hall before the bell
description: Feed the hall before the bell. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

ingredients.name: Thick-sliced brioche or Texas toast, cubed

steps.title: Layer the bread
steps.instruction: Cube bread into 1-inch pieces — day-old bread works best since it soaks without turning to mush. Spread evenly across two greased baking dishes.

steps.title: Whisk the custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs, milk, cream, sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla until fully combined. Pour evenly over the bread, pressing cubes down so every piece soaks.

steps.title: Rest before baking
steps.instruction: Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour, overnight is best, so the bread fully absorbs the custard — this is what keeps the center soft instead of dry.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Bake uncovered at 350°F for 45–50 minutes until the center is puffed and springs back and the edges are deep golden. A knife inserted in the center should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest, top, and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares. Brush with melted butter and a scatter of brown sugar. Serve warm with maple syrup on the side.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate French Toast Casserole with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Keep hot items on one side of the table and cold on the other — eggs stay hot, fruit stays cold.
Line up French Toast Casserole on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Feed the hall before the bell. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
